utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Please be seated. May we hear the case number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. This is Case Number IT-02-59-PT, the Prosecutor versus Darko Mrdja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances, please. For the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Nicholas Koumjian and Katharina Margetts, assisted by Gina Butler for the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, my name is Vojislav Dimitrijevic, attorney from Bosnia-Herzegovina. If you allow me, I proceed in my language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In your language. Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Today, the Status Conference was conferred in order to find out what is the actual state of the case. What about disclosure, the usual issues. But then later on, we have to come to the problem of on how to proceed in this case, the envisaged time limits, and so on. So therefore, I would ask the representative of the Office of Prosecutor, the accused arrived, and the initial appearance took place the 17th of June, 2002. Have there been any problems with the material to be disclosed to the other party?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, on the 17th of July, the supporting materials translated into the language of the accused, and also in English, were delivered through the Office of the OLAD to the registry to the accused. The additional disclosure feature would be additional witness statements, Rule 68 material, which searches have begun. And just a note, also a guide to the supporting material, we disclosed -- the supporting material was redacted. In the supporting material, the judge got redacted statements. We will provide the Defence counsel with unredacted material, that is, including the name of the witness. We're simply checking now with the witnesses to see if there's any particular witness protection issues before we disclose those names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I take the opportunity at this point in time to ask the accused in person whether he can follow the procedure in a language he understands.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, everything is all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask the Defence counsel, I got the document from the deputy registrar saying that you are assigned as of 5 July for a period of time of 120 days. And this was due to the fact that the registry has not yet received the declaration of means of the accused. Has this problem been settled in the past?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is true that I received that decision appointing me legal counsel to Mr. Mrdja. However, this problem is still outstanding. We are yet to submit the declaration of means for Mr. Mrdja so that the matter can be resolved under the rules of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And there are, as I understand from your answer, no problems between you and your client? There is a good relationship? The question is also for Mr. Mrdja in person. But from your point of view?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in the past two days I have succeeded in establishing contact with Mr. Mrdja, and I think our relationship is in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Mrdja, you share this view?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. Everything is fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then we can be sure that the proceedings can continue under the Rules. May I ask the OTP, being not in the possession of supporting material in this case, what will be the envisaged period of time at trial that this case will take? How many witnesses do you expect to call?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would anticipate that the trial would proceed -- the accused is charged with crimes against humanity, so one of the elements would be the widespread and systematic attacks. We anticipate that we would not be calling live witnesses to establish all of the elements of the widespread and systematic attacks. Assuming that that is done largely through either Rule 92 bis or through another means, stipulation or other means, the witnesses as to the incident in question, we anticipate no more than 15 witnesses would be called. And we think we can put this case on in four weeks or less on the Prosecution side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think this is important to discuss today. The accused and Defence counsel may know, or if they haven't already yet got this information. It causes problems to hear new cases as to the occupation of all the Trial Chambers and the courtroom facilities during the next month, if not years. Therefore, we have to take all the necessary measures to come as soon as possible to a solution. I don't know whether you are aware that Trial Chamber II at present is hearing the case against Dr. Stakic. This case covers, both in time and subject matter, also that what is the content of the indictment against Mr. Mrdja. To be very frank and open, it was to be considered by the Trial Chamber whether or not there could be a consecutive joinder with the Stakic case, but we came to the conclusion that this would not be a possibility granting all the rights to both Dr. Stakic and Mr. Mrdja. They deserve separate hearings so, therefore, separate hearings should be scheduled. On the other hand, we are obliged to hear the case as soon as possible. The concept of a fair trial includes also an expeditious trial. I know that we have numerous time limits and time frames before us, but we can only offer avoiding such a long period of waiting time for Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Mr. Mrdja. We can offer that the Trial Chamber would be prepared, during the break in the case against Dr. Stakic - this means between the end of the case of the Prosecutor and the start of the Defence case, if there is any - to hear the case we have before us in between. And we hear, it would be a period of time of four weeks and taking into account that here we have before us no doubt a serious, extremely serious, crime -- alleged crime against humanity. We have in Annex A the list of 228 persons missing from this incident at 21 August 1992. But nevertheless, in relation to other cases before us, it's limited, especially as regards the time. So therefore, our offer could be when the parties can come to an agreement to hear this case during this break I just mentioned before, and this would be somewhere after the 20th of September, 2002. We are, in the other case against Dr. Stakic, to a certain extent flexible, because in that case the Defence requests time for preparation of their case, so that coming to a conclusion. The case before us could be, on the basis of the goodwill of both parties, be heard between end of September and beginning of December. I don't know whether the parties had already the possibility in the past to contact and discuss how they want to proceed, especially what the Defence will be, what will be the Defence case, but I advise the parties, as time is of the essence, already today to contribute, to give their observations whether they are willing and prepared to act in this way. First of all, for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you very much for your comments. The Defence shares your opinion that in this case, a sooner trial date rather than a later one is advisable. However, we have only just been seized of the documents served on us by the Prosecution. The Defence has not still been consolidated in the sense that I have no co-counsel or assistants. However, we do support your proposal to schedule a trial date as soon as possible. But it is difficult for me to assess at this time how long the Defence will need to gather all the necessary information and evidence. It seems to me, though, with all due respect, and with certain reservations that the dates that you have just suggested could be acceptable to the Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the position of the OTP, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think -- I would like to think that it would be realistic for us to shoot for a starting date of October the 1st. As Your Honour knows, I'm engaged in Stakic, and it would be helpful at least to have a short break to prepare between the two cases. In addition, I should let the Defence know, there are a few other witness statements that were taken subsequent to the supporting materials put together, but they can be provided shortly. There also are many, many statements dealing with crimes in which the accused is named, Mr. Mrdja is named, which are not the subject of the indictment. I don't see a need to provide those and translate those to the accused. But if the Defence feels differently, we can talk about that. So I would say at this point, I would hope that we can shoot for the starting date of the 1st of October, and we would like very much to expeditiously try the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I am satisfied by the contributions of both parties because it's really important that we can avoid that Mr. Mrdja is in the Detention Unit for a period which could amount to a period of time which would be unproportional. And therefore, having heard your contributions, I really invite both parties to come as soon as possible already before the court recess together and try to find a solution. As I said earlier, the Trial Chamber is prepared to hear this case during the break. There would be one -- the one side may call it an advantage - to be quite honest with you - the other side may call it disadvantage, that there is a Trial Chamber being aware of the problems in Prijedor in 1992, especially in the period of time of the alleged crime we have before us. Therefore, I invite the parties as soon as possible to discuss those issues, whether or not it's possible to introduce as much as possible material, be it 92 bis statements or making use in this case of the possibility to take judicial notice or to come to agreed facts. Because in this case, it may be, indeed, for both parties an advantage to have Judges having heard already a lot about the environment this alleged crime probably has been committed. So therefore, I would like the parties to give the Tribunal in writing a notice whether or not, at the end of the next week or in the middle of the next week, they are prepared to proceed in this envisaged way because it would be necessary to ask the Secretary-General of the United Nations to assign the ad litem Judges also for this case, the case we have before us. This would be a prerequisite for hearing the case as fast as possible. And in addition, I would like the Office of the Prosecutor to provide also in this case the Trial Chamber with the necessary material, supporting material, that we know a little bit more than only having before us the indictment. We are acquainted in the way of working together and having access to this material from the Stakic case, and it should be done in the same way as it is done there. May I ask, are there any other observations as regards the proceedings in this case now from, first, from your point of view?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Before giving the floor to the Defence, I would ask the Defence counsel, you mentioned already the problem of co-counsel and investigator, to contact immediately the OLAD here in this premises to assist you in having co-counsel and an assistant as soon as possible that also for you the necessary is done that you can be prepared. Any other issues from your point of view to be raised today?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIMITRIJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then finally, before concluding this session, I have to ask the accused in person, do you have any problems as regards your health or the situation you're confronted with in the Detention Unit?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything is perfectly fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And you, of course, you are not obliged - to the contrary - you have the right, as I said to you during the initial appearance, you have the right to remain silent. But did you understand the procedure that was just discussed amongst the counsel in this case, that we tried to find as soon as possible a date for the hearing in your case?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understood what you talked about, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And you agree with this expeditious procedure?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with everything that my attorney has stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. This concludes today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: at 4.26 p.m.
